title: body_validator plugin config
description: The `config` object of an enabled `body_validator` plugin, generated from ferrum-edge/ferrum-edge openapi.yaml at v0.9.21 (f9915358c8032214f4034a17c28cdf72d14006c3), component BodyValidatorConfig and every component it references. Do not edit: run ci/plugin_config_schemas.py. This is Edge's own configuration schema, governed by Edge's support policy (docs/versioning.md); the plugin catalog records when Edge requires it.

BodyValidatorConfig.description: Plugin: body_validator — JSON Schema, XML, and gRPC protobuf validation for request/response bodies. Unknown top-level keys and unknown keys inside a protobuf_method_messages entry are rejected at construction, so a typo can never silently disable an intended rule; the plugin is fail-closed, and a rejected configuration keeps the last known-good generation. Configured JSON Schemas are compiled once at construction under an explicit draft, XML bodies are parsed by a real XML parser, and decoded protobuf messages must satisfy proto2 required-field initialization. Configuration errors use value-free field and category messages; supplied keys, paths, URIs, schema values, XML entries, and compiler diagnostics are not reproduced. Applicability follows the configured representation, never the request method: any request whose Content-Type matches content_types (or is application/grpc for protobuf configs) is buffered and validated, including GET, HEAD, OPTIONS, DELETE, PUT, PATCH, and non-standard methods. Once a configured rule applies, an empty, absent, or non-UTF-8 representation fails closed (400 request, 502 response) instead of being skipped, and native gRPC always runs frame validation. The only exemptions are protocol-defined: empty terminal gRPC error replies (a single valid non-zero grpc-status), and responses that carry no content by status/method semantics (1xx, 204, 205, 304, and responses to HEAD). Early before_proxy inspection prefers a rewritten UTF-8 request_body metadata view when present, falls back to raw buffered bytes when no text view exists, then the transport-proven-empty witness, and otherwise fails closed; the final request-body hook validates the exact backend-visible bytes. A request that declares a non-identity Content-Encoding is not judged early at all: the shared backend-visible representation gate decodes it under bounded, budget-charged limits and the final request-body hook validates the resulting plaintext before any byte reaches the backend, so a valid gzip JSON/XML upload succeeds while an undecodable coding is still refused. Representation-gap diagnostics are fixed strings and never echo body bytes. gRPC protobuf validation covers native gRPC and gRPC-Web (binary and text) framing in both directions, including a translated gRPC-Web response after the grpc_web plugin re-framed it; only methods a configured descriptor applies to are buffered, so unenrolled streaming RPCs keep streaming. Protobuf decoding is bounded before reflection (message, value, and 32-level depth budgets, for every descriptor pool) and its decompressed and reflected working set is charged to the aggregate decode budget; a budget refusal is a 503 / RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED capacity terminal. Response validation applies only to response_status_codes (default 2XX) and never to 206/226 fragments; an empty synthetic success (for example an empty response_mock body) is validated like an empty backend response. Every constraint below mirrors a runtime admission rule, so a configuration this schema accepts is one BodyValidator::new accepts, except for two dependencies that are node-local and cannot be expressed statically: protobuf_descriptor_path must name a readable FileDescriptorSet, and every configured message type must resolve inside it (and reject_unsupported_media_types paired only with response-direction protobuf_method_messages entries is refused at runtime).

json_schema.description: JSON Schema for request body validation. Compiled at plugin construction under json_schema_draft; a malformed schema, an unknown or unsupported keyword shape, an invalid type name, a non-local $ref/$dynamicRef, a non-fragment $id/id, a $vocabulary declaration, a $schema naming another draft, or a schema exceeding the 32-level / 20000-node budget fails construction. Reference and identifier policy applies only at actual schema positions; property/definition names and unreferenced literal annotation/instance objects are not interpreted as keywords. A supported local URI-fragment JSON Pointer makes its object/boolean target an actual schema even under a normally literal or unknown container; pointer percent-decoding, escaping, root handling, and cycles match the validator library. Draft 7 walks definitions but not $defs unless directly referenced; Draft 2020-12 walks both. Budgets count every JSON node in the supplied value.

json_schema_draft.description: JSON Schema dialect used to compile json_schema and response_json_schema. There is no auto-detect mode; a schema whose $schema names a different draft is rejected. $dynamicRef has reference semantics only under draft2020-12 and remains an unknown, inert keyword under draft7.

required_fields.description: Simple required field names in request body. Empty entries are rejected at construction; an empty list simply configures no required-field rule.

validate_xml.description: Enable XML well-formedness validation. The body must parse as a single well-formed XML document (one root element, valid names, attribute grammar and uniqueness, valid characters, declared entity references, no text outside the root). The original text is parsed without Unicode whitespace trimming. External SYSTEM/PUBLIC identifiers on the DOCTYPE or an entity declaration are always rejected; external entities are never retrieved.

required_xml_elements.description: Required XML element names, matched against parsed element names. A bare name matches that local name in any namespace; Clark notation ("{http://example.com/ns}item") requires the expanded namespace URI and local name to match, and "{}item" requires no namespace. An entry that opens Clark notation without closing it, or whose local name is empty or is not an XML NCName (no whitespace, markup, braces, or "prefix:local" spelling), is rejected at construction: the matcher compares against parsed local names, so such an entry could never be satisfied by any well-formed document.

xml_max_entities.description: Max <!ENTITY declarations allowed in an XML DOCTYPE before the body is rejected as a possible entity-expansion (billion-laughs) attack. Applies to request and response XML when well-formedness validation runs.

xml_reject_nested_entities.description: Reject XML whose entity definitions reference other general entities (the billion-laughs expansion signature). Entity declaration names and general/parameter entity references are read with the XML Name grammar, the same production the parser uses, so a non-ASCII entity name is subject to the restriction rather than invisible to it. When this is enabled, an entity declaration the policy cannot read a replacement text out of is refused outright rather than counted as safe.

content_types.description: Request media types to validate. Matching uses the Content-Type type/subtype essence only (parameters stripped, OWS trimmed, ASCII case-insensitive). An entry of the form type/*+suffix is an RFC 6838 structured-suffix pattern matching any type/name+suffix with a non-empty name (for example application/problem+json), except the gRPC-family types application/grpc+*, application/grpc-web+*, and application/grpc-web-text+*. Distinct neighbors such as application/json-seq and parameter values that merely contain a configured string do not match. An empty list is rejected (omit the field for the defaults), as are empty or parameter-only entries; malformed actual headers do not match and are skipped (or refused with 415 under reject_unsupported_media_types).

response_json_schema.description: JSON Schema for response body validation. Compiled at plugin construction under json_schema_draft with the same fail-closed rules as json_schema. Response-side violations are reported to the client without the rejected upstream value or its instance location.

response_required_fields.description: Required field names in response. Empty entries are rejected at construction; an empty list configures no required-field rule.

response_validate_xml.description: Enable response XML well-formedness validation with the same exact- text parsing and external DOCTYPE/entity identifier rejection as validate_xml.

response_required_xml_elements.description: Required XML element names in responses, with the same parsing, Clark-notation, and XML NCName admission rules as required_xml_elements.

response_content_types.description: Response media types to validate. Same type/subtype and structured-suffix pattern matching semantics as content_types (parameters stripped; neighbors, parameter collisions, and malformed headers do not match). An empty list is rejected.

response_status_codes.description: Upstream response statuses response validation applies to: exact integer statuses and/or status classes 1XX-5XX (case-insensitive X). Defaults to 2XX, so a backend error document (404, 422, 500, ...) keeps its own status and body instead of being judged against the success schema and replaced by a 502. Partial (206) and delta (226) responses are fragments and are never validated. An empty list is rejected.

enforcement_mode.description: block rejects violations (400 request, 415 unsupported request media type, 502 response). log_only evaluates every configured rule but always continues, never claims the shared representation gates (so a content-coded body is recorded as uninspected), and records the would-be outcome. In both modes a violation is published in transaction metadata as body_validator.request_outcome / body_validator.response_outcome (rejected, would_reject, uninspected, or capacity_refused) with the matching _status and payload-free _detail keys.

reject_unsupported_media_types.description: Refuse with 415 a request that carries a body no configured request rule inspects: a missing, malformed, or comma-joined Content-Type, a media type outside content_types, an allowlisted type no rule can inspect, or a gRPC request when no protobuf request rule is configured. Bodyless requests (proven by Content-Length 0 or by the buffered transport), CONNECT requests, and frontend-classified WebSocket handshakes are unaffected; a bare Upgrade header is not. Requires at least one request validation rule.

protobuf_descriptor_path.description: Node-local path to a compiled FileDescriptorSet binary (protoc --descriptor_set_out --include_imports). CP admission is shape-only; file/DP nodes validate the local dependency, and an unavailable runtime dependency fails applicable gRPC validation closed.

protobuf_request_type.description: Default fully-qualified protobuf message type for request validation. Requires protobuf_descriptor_path.

protobuf_response_type.description: Default fully-qualified protobuf message type for response validation. Requires protobuf_descriptor_path.

request.description: Fully-qualified protobuf message type for request validation

response.description: Fully-qualified protobuf message type for response validation

protobuf_method_messages.description: Per-method message type overrides keyed by gRPC path. Requires protobuf_descriptor_path. Each key must be the gRPC method path the hooks look up — '/package.Service/Method': one leading '/', exactly two non-empty segments, and no whitespace, control character, query, or fragment. A key spelled any other way could never be selected by the exact method lookup, so it is rejected rather than admitted as an inert rule. Each entry accepts only 'request' and 'response', must set at least one of them, and any other key rejects the configuration. An entry is direction-authoritative: a direction it omits is not validated for that method, rather than falling back to protobuf_request_type / protobuf_response_type. The method is the trailing /Service/Method of the bound backend-effective path, else (request side) the synthetic :path the native gRPC ladder injects, else grpc_full_method, else the request path, so prefixes and backend base paths cannot change which entry applies and per-method rules apply on HTTP/3 and every dispatcher.

protobuf_reject_unknown_fields.description: Reject messages containing field numbers not in the descriptor, at the top level and inside every present nested, repeated, map-value, oneof, and extension message value, in both directions, under the same bounded 32-level / 50000-message walk as the initialization check. A closed (proto2) enum is judged per wire occurrence: any occurrence outside the declared set is an unknown field (refused in either order, including packed, map-value, and extension values), and a required closed-enum field with only undeclared occurrences is unset; open proto3 enums keep any number. The rejection carries a count only, never a field number or payload byte. This is independent of proto2 required-field initialization, which is always enforced: a decoded message that omits any proto2 required field, at the top level or inside a present nested/repeated/map/extension message value, is rejected regardless of this setting.

grpc_max_decompressed_size_bytes.description: Maximum decompressed gRPC protobuf payload size in bytes for both request and response validation. Positive integer matching runtime `usize` parsing. Zero is rejected so compressed input is always bounded. When omitted, inherits `FERRUM_MAX_REQUEST_BODY_SIZE_BYTES` when that value parses as an unsigned integer; otherwise falls back to 10 MiB (10485760). Hard ceiling 67108864 (64 MiB): a larger configured value is rejected, and an environment-inherited value above it is clamped to it. No static OpenAPI default is advertised because the effective value can be environment-derived.
